body:
Remediated the 4 DEAD entries; the 30 suspect entries are left open as a
diagnosed systemic pattern rather than case-by-case link rot (see checklist).

**DEAD (4/4 addressed):**

- [x] 3x `wizkidsgames.com` Mage Knight PDFs (rulebook/walkthrough/FAQ) —
  confirmed dead (`ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID`; `curl -k` still shows the
  underlying HTTP 500 outage first flagged 2026-07-08). Each citing doc's
  `url` field now points directly at its already-known-good Wayback Machine
  snapshot (previously the dead URL was kept as `url`, with the snapshot
  only mentioned in `notes`). `src-NNN` ids unchanged, confidence unchanged
  (the official text itself is unaffected, only the origin host).
- [x] `github.com/no-trbl-2-u/game-knowledge-base/issues/1` (cited from
  `operations.okf.md`) — not actually link rot: this repo is private, so
  check-links' unauthenticated probe always 404s on issue pages. Verified
  via `gh issue view 1` that the issue exists (closed) and its body/comments
  still match the doc's Evidence quotes. Documented in the source's `notes`
  so future passes don't re-flag it.

**suspect (30, not individually remediated this pass):**

- [ ] ~27 of the 30 are `boardgamegeek.com` page fetches returning 401/403.
  Confirmed via both `curl` and `WebFetch` this pass (tested against
  marvel-champions, root, spirit-island, quacks BGG pages) — this is a
  systemic anti-bot block on BGG, not per-game rot. The pages are live; a
  scripted/headless fetch just can't reach them. Recommend the weekly
  check-links job stop escalating repeat BGG 403/401s as new findings once
  this pattern is established, and/or note in `OKF_SPEC.md` that BGG live
  metadata (rating/rank/weight refresh) needs a manual/browser-session pass,
  not automated retry.
  - `douglassun.substack.com`, `apps.apple.com`, `kickstarter.com` (3
    remaining) are likely the same class of anti-bot block (401/403/429);
    not yet individually confirmed.

Also fully drained the `needs_followup` backlog for **marvel-champions**
(worst offender: 9 of 11 docs were `needs_followup`, all downstream of one
root cause — the 2026-07-12 scout run's toolset couldn't extract the
official Rules Reference PDF or the lead review's full text). Retried this
pass with `WebFetch` + `pypdf`: both extractions succeeded cleanly. Rules
docs now carry real page-cited claims instead of stub placeholders; the
review/better-if docs are corrected to match the full source text (it
turned out to contradict two of the doc's original guessed opportunities —
see commit body). Only the BGG-metadata followup remains open for that game,
for the same systemic reason above.

6 more games (hoplomachus-remastered, legendary-encounters,
gi-joe-deck-building-game, oathsworn-into-the-deepwood, arkham-horror,
slay-the-spire) still carry smaller `needs_followup` backlogs from the same
BGG-block / PDF-extraction-tooling pattern; carrying those to next month's
pass per the audit's ~20-doc cap.

Leaving this issue open with the suspect checklist above; will close once
the BGG pattern is either fixed at the tooling level or formally accepted
as out-of-scope for automated remediation.
